candidates.statement: Let (A, ∆) be an aqg with analytic extension (Ar, ∆r). Then 1. (A, ∆) is compact and commutative iﬀthere exists a compact group G such that (Ar, ∆r) ∼= (C(G), ∆r). 2. (A, ∆) is discrete and cocommutative iﬀthere exists a compact group G such that (Ar, ∆r) ∼= (C∗ r (G), ∆r). Again these two cases are dual to each other. Here C(G) denotes the C*-algebra of continuous functions on G with uniform norm, whereas C∗ r (G) denotes the reduced group C*-algebra of G.
